{"unitId":"blue-3","x":2050,"y":1760,"facingDeg":0,"formation":"line","strength":188,"morale":68,"fatigue":15,"ammo":85,"status":"active","continuing":{"kind":"hold"},"orders":[{"orderId":"b3-1","result":"carried-out"}],"account":"Maj. Verneuil held the north end of the bridge as ordered and watched the road. When the enemy column came within carbine range and hussars appeared on its flank, he exchanged a few shots, then, being pressed by infantry as his orders foresaw, drew off over the bridge and re-formed behind the 1st Battalion. He would rather have charged, but obeyed.","departure":"Projection has the squadron stand at 100 m from a formed column and be shot down to 162 men and morale 29. Verneuil's orders say to fall back over the bridge if pressed by infantry, and the fast horse can cross 500 m in a couple of minutes, so he disengages after a brief exchange instead. Position, losses and morale therefore differ."},

"summary":"The Red vanguard column came down the high road and met the Blue cavalry picket at the north end of the bridge. After a short exchange of fire the picket, pressed by infantry as its orders foresaw, fell back over the bridge and re-formed behind the 1st Battalion. Red hussars rode on the column's right but could not cut it off. Red-1 halted at the bridge head and Red-3 on the river bank. Blue infantry held their line south of the river, out of range. Losses were light: about 12 Red infantry and about 12 Blue horse. The projection kept the cavalry standing and destroyed it; the umpire let it obey its orders to withdraw."}
